reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a robust quasi-periodic oscillation with an estimated fundamental period of ~95 points, visible as repeating waveforms across all candidates. Each cycle contains a sharp, narrow trough (duration ~5–10 points) followed by a slower, smoother recovery phase (~30–40 points), forming an asymmetric sawtooth-like motif. Amplitude (90th percentile range) is consistently ~1.8–2.0 in robust-standardized units, with median levels drifting gradually: candidate 0 sits near +0.88, candidates 1–2 near +0.2 to −0.16, and candidate 3 near −0.79—reflecting the underlying linear trend (slope ≈ −0.0002 per point). Noise is low-magnitude, high-frequency jitter (<0.2 std) superimposed on the main waveform; no sustained outliers or abrupt level shifts occur within clean segments. Baseline stability is moderate: slow monotonic drift dominates over short-term variance, and curvature is mild (0.02–0.07), indicating gentle convex/concave modulation of the envelope. Peaks are rounded and broad; troughs are sharper and more consistent in depth and width. Acceptable variation includes: (i) ±0.3 shift in median level across windows due to trend, (ii) slight widening/narrowing of troughs, (iii) minor changes in recovery slope, and (iv) occasional small secondary inflections near peak shoulders. Boundary truncation is minimal; all candidates show full cycles without artificial cutoffs.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidate 0 for queries with ≤1 cycle or high-stability requirements (e.g., detecting subtle shape distortions). Use candidates 2 or 3 for multi-cycle queries (>2 cycles) due to richer morphological context; candidate 2 is optimal when baseline is near zero, candidate 3 when baseline is negative. Avoid relying solely on candidate 1 if query shows no flat plateau—its mid-window hold is non-consensus and could mislead anomaly scoring.
uncertainties: Exact trough width tolerance (5–12 pts) not quantified; may vary with amplitude scaling
Whether the flat segment in candidate 1 is systemic or isolated remains ambiguous without labels
Quadratic/cubic trend contributions are small but may cause subtle envelope warping over >5 cycles
